title: First mid-air collision of airliners
summary: A British de Havilland DH.18A flying mail from Croydon to Paris collided in mid-air with a French Farman F.60 Goliath carrying passengers from Paris to Croydon near Thieuloy-Saint-Antoine. Operating in drizzle and fog with poor visibility at approximately 4000 feet, the two aircraft suddenly encountered each other with no time for evasive action. The DH.18 lost a wing and tail impacting first; the Goliath crashed minutes later. All seven occupants were killed, including the boy steward who died from injuries after initial rescue.
probable_cause: The collision occurred in foggy conditions with poor visibility. The two aircraft on converging routes suddenly encountered each other without warning or time for pilots to take evasive action.

factors.evidence: Following the normal route in drizzle and fog with poor visibility
The two aircraft suddenly encountered each other in the mist, neither having time to take evasive action
the DH.18A collided with the Goliath over Thieuloy-Saint-Antoine; the DH.18 lost a wing and the tail, and impacted first

events.text: On 7 April 1922, G-EAWO was flying mail from Croydon bound for Le Bourget, Paris, with only the pilot and a boy steward aboard
The Goliath (F-GEAD) piloted by M. Mire had departed Le Bourget with three passengers and a mechanic bound for Croydon
The DH.18A collided with the Goliath over Thieuloy-Saint-Antoine in the mist; during the collision the DH.18 lost a wing and the tail, and impacted first

title: Potez VII F-FRAV aviation accident
summary: Potez VII aircraft F-FRAV accident at Supí skály in Czechoslovakia on October 30, 1922.

events.text: Potez VII aircraft F-FRAV crashed at Supí skály resulting in one fatality.
